chapters.title: The Friendship Formula
chapters.sourcePressure: The source sidecar frames friendship as a four-part model: proximity, frequency, duration, and intensity. It stresses nonthreatening proximity, intensity as emotional glue, and the ethical edge that the same levers can deepen unhealthy influence.
chapters.coreMove: Diagnose a relationship by separating proximity, frequency, duration, and intensity before deciding what to strengthen or reduce.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the formula as a magic closeness recipe or assuming more contact always improves a bond.

chapters.title: Getting Noticed Before a Word Is Spoken
chapters.sourcePressure: The ch02 source centers first impressions and friend signals: eyebrow flash, head tilt, smile, and open posture reduce perceived threat before words can help. It also warns that signals open the door but do not create lasting trust alone.
chapters.coreMove: Use low-threat nonverbal cues to make the first seconds of contact feel safe enough for conversation to begin.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating friend signals as charisma tricks that guarantee rapport without later substance.

chapters.title: The Golden Rule of Friendship
chapters.sourcePressure: The ch03 source states the Golden Rule of Friendship: if you want people to like you, make them feel good about themselves. It warns against ego, flattery, and obvious performance.
chapters.coreMove: Shift attention outward so the other person leaves the interaction feeling better about themselves, not impressed by you.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing the rule to compliments, agreement, or self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Laws of Attraction
chapters.sourcePressure: The ch04 source widens from immediate liking into attraction through repeated contact, reciprocity, self-disclosure, and support. It warns that frequency cannot fix one-sided support or premature intimacy.
chapters.coreMove: Read attraction as a paced system of repeated contact, reciprocity, calibrated self-disclosure, and supportive responsiveness.
chapters.commonMisread: Collapsing attraction into romance, frequency, or fast disclosure.

chapters.title: Speaking the Language of Friendship
chapters.sourcePressure: The ch05 source anchors active listening, empathic statements, and responsive follow-up. It warns that empathy fails when it sounds scripted, intrusive, or self-serving.
chapters.coreMove: Turn conversation toward listening, empathic statements, and responsive follow-up so the other person feels heard rather than handled.
chapters.commonMisread: Mistaking active listening for parroting words, instant advice, or technique-heavy empathy.

chapters.title: Building Closeness
chapters.sourcePressure: The ch06 source centers common ground, reciprocal self-disclosure, and trust pacing. It warns that disclosure alone cannot create closeness if reciprocity is missing or similarity is forced.
chapters.coreMove: Build closeness by finding real common ground and pacing self-disclosure so trust grows through mutual evidence.
chapters.commonMisread: Assuming closeness comes from telling more, faster, or inventing similarity to speed trust.

chapters.title: Nurturing and Sustaining Long-Term Relationships
chapters.sourcePressure: The ch07 source is narrower and stresses maintenance, reciprocity, and repair. It warns that close relationships erode when care becomes assumed, one-sided, or delayed until crisis.
chapters.coreMove: Keep a bond durable by making reciprocity, maintenance, and early repair visible after closeness already exists.
chapters.commonMisread: Thinking a strong bond runs on history, loyalty, or familiarity without current upkeep.

chapters.title: The Perils and Promise of Relationships
chapters.sourcePressure: The ch08 source closes on trust, truth bias, online deception, and guarded optimism. It must preserve both relationship promise and risk without collapsing into cynicism or naive warmth.
chapters.coreMove: Pair openness with verification so trust grows at the speed of evidence rather than the speed of good feeling.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the warning into total suspicion, or treating warm signals and polished online presentation as proof.
